title: Flip the First K of Every 2K
statement:
You get a string s and an integer k. Cut s into blocks of 2k characters, starting from the front; the last block may be shorter. In every block, reverse the first k characters and leave the rest alone.

If the last block has fewer than k characters, reverse all of them. Return the resulting string.

examples.why: Block "abcdef" becomes "cba" + "def". The last block "gh" is shorter than 3, so all of it flips to "hg".
Block "abcd" becomes "ba" + "cd". The last block "e" flips to itself.
The whole string is one short block, so all of it is reversed.

constraints: s has only lowercase English letters
hints: The blocks start at indexes 0, 2k, 4k, … Visit only those starts.
From a start i, the part to reverse ends at min(i + k, n) − 1. Swap inward from both ends of that range.

explain.intuition:
The three rules in the statement are really one rule: from each block start i, reverse the range [i, min(i + k, n) − 1]. If at least k characters remain, that is the first k; otherwise it is whatever is left.

Strings are immutable in JavaScript and Python, so copy into an array, reverse each range in place with two pointers, and join once at the end.
steps: For i = 0, 2k, 4k, … while i < n: set lo = i, hi = min(i + k, n) − 1.
Swap a[lo] and a[hi], move both inward, until they meet.
pitfalls: Using i + k − 1 as the end without capping it at n − 1. The last short block then swaps with undefined.
Stepping by k instead of 2k, which reverses every block instead of every other one.
Building the result with string concatenation inside the loop, which can turn quadratic.

solutions.title: Slice and reverse
solutions.idea: Walk the string in 2k steps, append the reversed first k characters and the untouched next k.

solutions.title: Two pointers on a character array
solutions.idea: Reverse each range [i, min(i + k, n) − 1] in place by swapping from both ends.

followups: Reverse every word of a sentence in place, keeping the word order. Which part of this solution carries over?
Do the same on a linked list of characters: reverse the first k nodes of every 2k.
